new_jobs.title: Environmental Remediation Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

At Jacobs, we're focused on solving today's environmental challenges by delivering innovative and sustainable solutions for our clients and communities. We are seeking an experienced Project Manager to lead environmental investigation, remediation, compliance, and asset-retirement projects for upstream oil and gas clients, as well as government and private-sector environmental programs throughout New Mexico and the western United States.

Based in Albuquerque, New Mexico you'll serve as a key leader within our growing environmental practice, overseeing project execution from planning through closure while managing multidisciplinary project teams. This role will provide direct supervision and mentorship to junior technical staff, including environmental scientists, engineers, geologists, and field technicians supporting environmental remediation and asset-retirement activities.

You'll be responsible for delivering complex environmental projects involving upstream oil and gas facilities, wellsites, production infrastructure, pipeline assets, facility decommissioning, site investigations, remediation programs, regulatory compliance, and closure activities. Working directly with clients, regulators, subcontractors, and Jacobs technical specialists, you'll ensure projects are delivered safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with client objectives and regulatory requirements.

Key responsibilities include project planning and execution, client relationship management, scope and budget development, proposal preparation, subcontractor procurement and management, contract administration, financial performance tracking, invoicing, risk management, technical review, resource planning, and staff development. You'll maintain regular communication with clients and regulatory agencies while helping identify and pursue new business opportunities within the environmental and energy sectors.

In this role, you'll balance project delivery with team leadership, ensuring junior staff receive appropriate guidance, mentorship, and opportunities for professional growth. Safety will remain your highest priority as you promote Jacobs' culture of caring and excellence across all field and office operations.

At Jacobs, we're partnering across the globe to create the best project outcomes by maximizing the design, digital technology, and support capabilities of our Global Integrated Delivery (GID) teams. By joining Jacobs, you'll collaborate with technical experts across the company while helping grow a high-performing environmental project delivery team in New Mexico.

This is a hybrid position that combines office leadership, client engagement, project site visits, and remote work flexibility as needed to support project delivery and business objectives.

Key Responsibilities

Lead environmental investigation, remediation, compliance, and asset-retirement projects for upstream oil and gas clients and other industrial, commercial, and government clients.
Serve as the primary day-to-day point of contact for clients, maintaining strong working relationships and ensuring client satisfaction.
Manage project scope, schedule, budget, forecasting, invoicing, and overall financial performance.
Direct and mentor a team consisting of environmental scientists, engineers, geologists, and field technicians.
Supervise and support the Entry-Level Environmental Engineer/Scientist and Entry-Level Field Technician positions assigned to the New Mexico asset-retirement program.
Develop work plans, proposals, cost estimates, schedules, and subcontractor scopes of work.
Coordinate field activities including site characterization, environmental sampling, remediation system operation and maintenance, construction oversight, excavation, and closure activities.
Oversee subcontractor procurement, contracting, mobilization, performance, and safety.
Interface with state and federal regulatory agencies and support permit compliance activities.
Review and approve technical reports, work plans, closure reports, and regulatory submittals.
Support business development efforts through client engagement, proposal preparation, and identification of follow-on opportunities.
Promote a strong safety culture and ensure compliance with Jacobs and client health and safety requirements.
Collaborate with Jacobs Global Integrated Delivery teams and technical specialists to deliver high-quality project outcomes.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science, or a related field.
8+ years of progressively responsible experience managing environmental projects.
Demonstrated experience managing environmental investigation, remediation, compliance, or restoration projects for private or government clients.
Experience supporting upstream oil and gas facilities, wellsites, production assets, gathering systems, pipelines, asset-retirement programs, or energy-sector environmental projects.
Proven experience managing project budgets, schedules, contracts, and multidisciplinary project teams.
Experience supervising, mentoring, and developing junior technical staff.
Strong client communication and relationship management skills.
Experience preparing proposals, scopes of work, and cost estimates.
Knowledge of state and federal environmental regulations and permitting frameworks.
Ability to travel periodically to project sites throughout New Mexico and surrounding states.
Valid driver's license and acceptable driving record.
Current 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification with annual refreshers.

Ideally, You'll Also Have

Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
New Mexico environmental consulting experience.
Experience managing large-scale asset retirement, facility closure, or decommissioning programs.
Experience with remediation design, corrective action implementation, and construction oversight.
Experience working directly with upstream oil and gas operators on closure liabilities, environmental compliance, and reclamation programs.
Established client relationships within the New Mexico energy, environmental, or industrial markets.
Experience leading proposal capture efforts and developing new business opportunities.
Strong understanding of Jacobs project delivery systems and financial performance metrics.

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

new_jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD100617

Position Overview

Autodesk is shaping the future of the design and make industries by helping our customers navigate a rapidly evolving AI-driven landscape. As part of our Research team, you will help us understand how artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, and new business models are reshaping the competitive landscape across Manufacturing, AECO (Architecture, Engineering, Construction, and Operations), and Media and Entertainment.

This is an experienced individual contributor role on a small, highly collaborative team. You will support market and competitive intelligence work across Autodesk Research while independently leading selected projects and workstreams. Competitive intelligence is a team effort, and you will need to move comfortably between leading, contributing, and supporting depending on the needs of each project.

You will help Research teams understand the markets they are working in, turn complex information into clear recommendations, and improve the systems and processes that allow the team to take on more work. You will use AI and automation tools to work more efficiently while applying judgment about when deeper analysis, validation, or human expertise is needed.

Location: We support hybrid work, and you work near our Boston, Massachusetts, Toronto, Canada, or San Francisco, CA offices. This role follows East Coast hours.

Responsibilities

Conduct market and competitive analysis across Autodesk's industries, tracking signals such as AI developments, competitors, startups, funding, talent movement, product releases, partnerships, research, and regulatory changes
Distinguish meaningful change from noise and communicate clearly when the evidence does not support a new conclusion
Partner with Research teams to define target markets, map competitive landscapes, size opportunities, identify gaps, and test market and commercial assumptions
Take the lead on coordinating research and intelligence projects as needed, bringing structure to ambiguous questions, facilitating discussions, managing contributors and timelines, keeping teams on track, and ensuring conclusions are captured in clear final deliverables
Synthesize qualitative and quantitative information into clear points of view, challenging assumptions, reconciling conflicting perspectives, and connecting findings to broader implications for Autodesk
Produce recurring competitive intelligence and fast-turn analysis for leaders, translating complex market and technical developments into concise, executive-ready briefs, presentations, and market maps
Own the operating discipline for the team's intelligence work, managing priorities, timelines, research systems, source quality, and follow-through while improving processes that make the team more efficient and scalable
Use AI tools to accelerate research, analysis, and content development while applying judgment about when human verification, primary research, or subject matter expertise is required

Minimum Qualifications

5+ years of experience in competitive intelligence, market research, business intelligence, strategy, or a related analytical field
Strong analytical judgment and the ability to turn incomplete or fragmented information into a defensible point of view
Experience with market analysis, competitive research, market sizing, customer or expert research, or commercial opportunity assessment
Demonstrated ability to independently lead projects or significant workstreams involving multiple stakeholders and deadlines
Proven ability to collaborate effectively on analytical work, including contributing to projects led by others and bringing together different perspectives into a coherent output
Strong organizational skills and experience improving a process, workflow, or system
Experience with structured research tools such as Airtable and market data sources such as PitchBook, CB Insights, Crunchbase, or similar platforms
Professional experience using AI tools in research or analytical workflows, with an understanding of where additional validation or human review is required
Strong writing, communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex information clearly to senior stakeholders
Bachelor's degree in business, economics, data science, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with Manufacturing, AECO, or Media and Entertainment
Experience supporting research, incubation, innovation, product strategy, or new business initiatives
Experience with customer discovery, market validation, go-to-market analysis, or business case development
Working knowledge of AI and machine learning concepts and their business implications
Experience with Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, or similar analytical tools
MBA or equivalent business experience

Learn More

About Autodesk

Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you’re an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

Benefits

From health and financial benefits to time away and everyday wellness, we give Autodeskers the best, so they can do their best work. Learn more about our benefits in the U.S. by visiting https://benefits.autodesk.com/

Salary transparency

Salary is one part of Autodesk’s competitive compensation package. For U.S.-based roles, we expect a starting base salary between $83,000 and $148,830. Offers are based on the candidate’s experience and geographic location, and may exceed this range. In addition to base salaries, our compensation package may include annual cash bonuses, commissions for sales roles, stock grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Equal Employment Opportunity

At Autodesk, we're building a diverse workplace and an inclusive culture to give more people the chance to imagine, design, and make a better world. Autodesk is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic. new_jobs.description:
We exist to create positive change for people and the planet. Join us and make a difference too!

Job Title: Business Intelligence Analyst

Location: USA—Remote

About The Role

This role will act as an intelligence analyst for BSI Supply Chain Solutions division providing analysis to government and commercial clients. Further, this role is responsible for collecting information, analyzing data, and generating intelligence. This position will also serve as backup support for all supply chain security functions.

Responsibilities

Direct involvement in developing and supporting supply chain security solutions and services for BSI commercial and government clients through the collection of intelligence data
Identify and extract essential information from intelligence sources, research, and investigations; analyze the data and synthesize the information into written reports that can be disseminated to BSI government and commercial clients through BSI products and services
Develop specific expertise, discern patterns of complex behaviors, and provide an accurate understanding of present and emerging threats to supply chain security
Subject matter will have particular emphasis on terrorism activities, cargo disruption trends, supply chain security, industrial, governmental, cultural, and other demographic trade security-related indicators
Efficiently manage and navigate records, reports, databases, and other sources of information to support research and analysis
Retain a heightened sense of awareness of compliance and client confidentiality obligations

To Be Successful In The Role, You Will Have

Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, International Affairs, Supply Chain or relevant field required
Knowledge of administrative and clerical procedures and systems such as word processing, managing files and records, designing forms, and other office procedures and terminology
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills to provide internal customer service at all levels of the business
1 year previous work experience

What We Offer

BSI offers a competitive total reward package, an independent and varied job in an international environment, flexible working hours, ongoing training and development with the inclusion of 20-days annual leave, bank holidays, medical, dental, vision, and life insurance, 401(K) with company contribution, short-term and long-term disability, maternal leave, paid parental leave, paid bereavement leave, learning and development opportunities, and a wide range of flexible benefits that you can tailor to suit your lifestyle.

The Cybersecurity Analyst II performs advanced information security analysis with a focus on cloud security, web application protection, and governance, risk, and compliance activities. The position supports both on‑premises and cloud environments by evaluating, implementing, and monitoring security controls to prevent unauthorized access, modification, or disclosure of information resources.

The analyst conducts security assessments and risk-based needs assessments across assigned systems. Responsibilities include assisting with the development of System Security Plans (SSPs), documenting vulnerabilities and corrective actions, analyzing administrative, technical, and operational controls, and preparing audit documentation, formal reports, and leadership‑level reporting.

The role also provides advisory services to business partners, offering guidance on secure architecture, secure application development practices, and cloud configuration requirements. The analyst maintains compliance and risk artifacts in a Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platform, supports Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities, and delivers targeted security training to agency stakeholders. Work is performed under limited supervision with significant latitude for independent judgment.

Essential Job Functions (EJFs)

Attends work on a regular and predictable schedule in accordance with agency leave policy and performs other duties as assigned.

Security and Risk Management Services (30%)
Provides security and risk management services by performing risk identification, assessment, and remediation, as well as regulatory and internal compliance monitoring; uses established standards and processes to adequately protect Health and Human Services (HHS) personnel, facilities, cloud infrastructure, information, and business operations.
Performs cyclical and periodic technology risk assessments of cloud environments such as Microsoft Azure and Amazon Web Services (AWS) and on‑premises environments; reviews technology use within business initiatives; conducts web application security analysis, vulnerability analysis, and evaluates emerging threats.
Facilitates risk assessment sessions with Information Owners and Custodians; identifies and documents threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, impact, and mitigation strategies; records risks, exceptions, and Risk-Based Decisions in a GRC tool; validates vulnerability scan results, prioritizes findings, and tracks remediation.
System Security Planning (25%)
Assist with the development of System Security Plans (SSPs) for systems and applications in alignment with applicable state and federal requirements.
Collaborates with program teams, Information Owners, and Custodians to collect, validate, and document security control implementation evidence.
Ensures Security System Plans align with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-53, NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF), Department of Information Resources (DIR) standards, and agency CISO policies.
Security and Risk-Based Needs Assessments (25%)
Plans and conducts security assessments to evaluate the effectiveness of administrative, technical, and operational security controls across assigned systems; reviews and analyzes supporting documentation and evidence.
Documents assessment results, prepares formal reports, and tracks remediation and corrective actions such as Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms) to completion.
Performs risk-based needs assessments of automated systems to identify information security requirements; evaluates agency systems including infrastructure, processes, and procedures with a specific focus on cloud security posture management (CSPM) and web application vulnerabilities to discover compliance needs and gaps.
Provides Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Continuous Monitoring, Advisory, and Training Support (15%)
Maintains security artifacts, risk records, POA&Ms, continuous monitoring evidence, and compliance documentation within a GRC tool such as RSA Archer; supports Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities and ongoing monitoring requirements to ensure systems remain compliant with regulatory and agency security standards.
Prepares documentation, reporting packages, and audit responses for internal reviews, external audits, and leadership inquiries.
Advises management and users regarding enterprise security program functions, including cloud security best practices and secure application development standards; provides targeted training to agency customers within assigned specific security domains.
Performs or leads other duties as assigned. (5%)

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities (KSAs)

Ability to advise diverse stakeholders on secure architecture, secure application development standards, and cloud security best practices; ability to deliver focused security training.
Ability to prepare audit documentation, assessment reports, Authorization to Operate (ATO) packages, and leadership reporting with clear, concise communication.
Skill in risk analysis and vulnerability management, including validation and prioritization of scan results and tracking remediation to closure.
Skill in conducting security and risk-based needs assessments of automated systems and business initiatives; ability to analyze administrative, technical, and operational controls and supporting evidence.
Knowledge of enterprise Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) platforms such as RSA Archer; skill in maintaining risk records, POA&Ms, exceptions, and continuous monitoring evidence.
Knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 control families, NIST RMF steps, DIR security control standards, and agency CISO policies; skill in applying control requirements to systems and documenting implementation within SSPs.
Knowledge of cloud security posture management (CSPM) concepts and tooling; ability to evaluate cloud configurations for misconfigurations and control gaps across Azure and AWS environments.

Registrations, Licensure Requirements Or Certifications

Prefer one or more of the following certifications:

CompTIA Security+
Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA)
Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP)
Global Information Assurance Certification (GIAC) or similar security certifications.

Initial Screening Criteria

Graduation from an accredited four-year college or university with major coursework in information technology security, computer information systems, computer science, management information systems, or a related field is generally preferred.

Education and experience may be substituted for one another on a year for year basis.

Conhecimento sólido em técnicas de exploração (web, rede, infraestrutura, Active Directory)

new_jobs.title: Market and Competitive Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Job Requisition ID #

26WD100617

Position Overview

Autodesk is shaping the future of the design and make industries by helping our customers navigate a rapidly evolving AI-driven landscape. As part of our Research team, you will help us understand how artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, and new business models are reshaping the competitive landscape across Manufacturing, AECO (Architecture, Engineering, Construction, and Operations), and Media and Entertainment.

This is an experienced individual contributor role on a small, highly collaborative team. You will support market and competitive intelligence work across Autodesk Research while independently leading selected projects and workstreams. Competitive intelligence is a team effort, and you will need to move comfortably between leading, contributing, and supporting depending on the needs of each project.

You will help Research teams understand the markets they are working in, turn complex information into clear recommendations, and improve the systems and processes that allow the team to take on more work. You will use AI and automation tools to work more efficiently while applying judgment about when deeper analysis, validation, or human expertise is needed.

Location: We support hybrid work, and you work near our Boston, Massachusetts, Toronto, Canada, or San Francisco, CA offices. This role follows East Coast hours.

Responsibilities

Conduct market and competitive analysis across Autodesk's industries, tracking signals such as AI developments, competitors, startups, funding, talent movement, product releases, partnerships, research, and regulatory changes
Distinguish meaningful change from noise and communicate clearly when the evidence does not support a new conclusion
Partner with Research teams to define target markets, map competitive landscapes, size opportunities, identify gaps, and test market and commercial assumptions
Take the lead on coordinating research and intelligence projects as needed, bringing structure to ambiguous questions, facilitating discussions, managing contributors and timelines, keeping teams on track, and ensuring conclusions are captured in clear final deliverables
Synthesize qualitative and quantitative information into clear points of view, challenging assumptions, reconciling conflicting perspectives, and connecting findings to broader implications for Autodesk
Produce recurring competitive intelligence and fast-turn analysis for leaders, translating complex market and technical developments into concise, executive-ready briefs, presentations, and market maps
Own the operating discipline for the team's intelligence work, managing priorities, timelines, research systems, source quality, and follow-through while improving processes that make the team more efficient and scalable
Use AI tools to accelerate research, analysis, and content development while applying judgment about when human verification, primary research, or subject matter expertise is required

Minimum Qualifications

5+ years of experience in competitive intelligence, market research, business intelligence, strategy, or a related analytical field
Strong analytical judgment and the ability to turn incomplete or fragmented information into a defensible point of view
Experience with market analysis, competitive research, market sizing, customer or expert research, or commercial opportunity assessment
Demonstrated ability to independently lead projects or significant workstreams involving multiple stakeholders and deadlines
Proven ability to collaborate effectively on analytical work, including contributing to projects led by others and bringing together different perspectives into a coherent output
Strong organizational skills and experience improving a process, workflow, or system
Experience with structured research tools such as Airtable and market data sources such as PitchBook, CB Insights, Crunchbase, or similar platforms
Professional experience using AI tools in research or analytical workflows, with an understanding of where additional validation or human review is required
Strong writing, communication, and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex information clearly to senior stakeholders
Bachelor's degree in business, economics, data science, computer science, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with Manufacturing, AECO, or Media and Entertainment
Experience supporting research, incubation, innovation, product strategy, or new business initiatives
Experience with customer discovery, market validation, go-to-market analysis, or business case development
Working knowledge of AI and machine learning concepts and their business implications
Experience with Excel, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, or similar analytical tools
MBA or equivalent business experience

Learn More

About Autodesk

Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you’re an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

Benefits

From health and financial benefits to time away and everyday wellness, we give Autodeskers the best, so they can do their best work. Learn more about our benefits in the U.S. by visiting https://benefits.autodesk.com/

Salary transparency

Salary is one part of Autodesk’s competitive compensation package. For U.S.-based roles, we expect a starting base salary between $83,000 and $148,830. Offers are based on the candidate’s experience and geographic location, and may exceed this range. In addition to base salaries, our compensation package may include annual cash bonuses, commissions for sales roles, stock grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Equal Employment Opportunity

At Autodesk, we're building a diverse workplace and an inclusive culture to give more people the chance to imagine, design, and make a better world. Autodesk is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status or any other legally protected characteristic. We also consider for employment all qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with applicable law.

Belonging

We take pride in cultivating a culture of belonging where everyone can thrive. Learn more here: https://www.autodesk.com/company/global-belonging

In-Person Onboarding and Identity Verification

Moody’s is transforming how the world sees risk. As a global leader in ratings and integrated risk assessment, we’re advancing AI to move from insight to action—enabling intelligence that not only understands complexity but responds to it. We decode risk to unlock opportunity, helping our clients navigate uncertainty with clarity, speed, and confidence.

If you are excited about this opportunity but do not meet every single requirement, please apply! You still may be a great fit for this role or other open roles. We are seeking candidates who model our values: invest in every relationship, lead with curiosity, champion diverse perspectives, turn inputs into actions, and uphold trust through integrity.

Skills and Competencies

0-2 years’ experience in credit/financial data analysis and interpretation with knowledge of capital markets; experience in structured finance will be an added advantage
Skilled in identifying key credit risk factors and applying relevant credit methodologies to support analysis and decision-making.
Excellent Microsoft Office skills, particularly advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Excellent English communication and interpersonal skills
Detail-oriented and well-organized, with a proven ability to excel in team-driven environments.
Basic understanding of AI concepts (Generative AI tools and Agentic AI systems), with curiosity and enthusiasm for learning how AI tools can be used to improve processes and drive efficiency leveraging these technologies for research, analysis, or workflow optimization. Interest in exploring AI systems and a willingness to develop awareness of responsible AI practices, including risk management and ethical use.

Education

Analyze financial reports, official statements, and related documents to assess issuer performance and creditworthiness.

new_jobs.title: Institutional Biosafety Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Join us and make YOUR mark on the World!

Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) has turned bold ideas into world-changing impact advancing science and technology to strengthen U.S. security and promote global stability.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. With a culture built on innovation and operational excellence, LLNL is a place where your expertise can make a real impact.

Job Description

We have an opening for an Institutional Biosafety Program Manager
to provide strategic and technical leadership for LLNL’s institutional biosafety program. In this role, you will manage the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of a comprehensive biosafety program supporting biological research, laboratory animal research, and related institutional review activities.

You will work closely with Environment, Safety and Health leadership, principal investigators, research teams, institutional committees, and the Department of Energy to ensure that biological research is conducted safely, securely, and in compliance with applicable federal, state, local, and Laboratory requirements.

This position is in the Occupational Safety, Health and Environmental Protection Department within the Environment, Safety and Health Directorate.

This position offers a hybrid schedule, blending in-person and virtual presence. The ability to work from home one or more days per week may be available after a probationary period.

You will

Manage and continuously improve LLNL’s institutional biosafety program, policies, procedures, and program documentation.
Provide expert technical guidance on biosafety, biosecurity, biological research risks, containment concepts, and laboratory operations.
Develop program strategies, priorities, performance objectives, and resource requirements aligned with Laboratory mission needs.
Lead risk assessments for new and ongoing biological research activities and support development of Biological Use Authorizations.
Oversee biosafety reviews involving biological agents and materials, including activities conducted at BSL-1 through BSL-3 and ABSL-1 through ABSL-3 containment levels.
Ensure compliance with applicable requirements and industry standards, including Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories, NIH Guidelines, OSHA standards, DOE requirements, and other applicable federal, state and local regulations.
Serve as the Institutional Biosafety Officer and participate as a voting member of the Institutional Biosafety Committee, Biological Review Committee, Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee and Institutional Review Entity.
Serve as an institutional technical liaison with DOE, the DOE Livermore Field Office, USDA, and other regulatory or oversight organizations.
Oversee biosafety audits, inspections, assessments, investigations, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
Develop and maintain emergency response procedures for incidents involving biological agents and materials.
Oversee institutional biosafety training, including curriculum development, regulatory updates, delivery, and compliance tracking.
Establish and maintain data-driven performance measures, leading indicators, and program health metrics.
Compile, analyze, and communicate biosafety program information for leadership, oversight bodies, committees, and regulatory agencies.
Provide biosafety input into the planning, renovation, and design of biological research facilities.
Build collaborative relationships with principal investigators, researchers, line managers, staff, committees, and external stakeholders.
Benchmark biosafety practices with other DOE laboratories and research institutions.
Lead, mentor, and develop biosafety professionals and other program personnel, as assigned.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship.
Ph.D. in biology, microbiology, molecular biology, virology, immunology, or a related life sciences field, or an equivalent combination of education and substantial relevant experience.
Extensive experience managing or leading institutional biosafety programs in a research laboratory, biotechnology, government, or comparable environment.
Expert knowledge of biosafety principles, laboratory operations, pathogenic microbiological techniques, biological containment, and biological hazard controls.
Expert knowledge of applicable biosafety regulations, standards, and guidelines, including BMBL, NIH Guidelines, OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens requirements, and relevant DOE requirements.
Substantial experience with biosafety or voting membership in relevant biogovernance committees such as IBC, IRE, IACUC, or equivalent committees.
Demonstrated experience conducting or overseeing biological research risk assessments, laboratory inspections, audits, incident investigations, and corrective action programs.
Experience developing policies, procedures, training programs, performance measures, reports, and other institutional program documents.
Demonstrated ability to interpret highly complex or ambiguous regulatory requirements and apply them across diverse research and operational environments.
Experience managing resources, projects, priorities, budgets, or personnel within a complex organization.
Excellent communication, facilitation, collaboration, negotiation, presentation, and conflict-resolution skills.
Strong analytical, organizational, situational awareness, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Demonstrated ability to build trust, gain consensus, and influence personnel at all levels while maintaining high standards of safety and compliance.

Qualifications We Desire

Current certification or registration through the American Biological Safety Association, such as Certified Biological Safety Professional or Registered Biosafety Professional.
Experience working at the BSL-3 or ABSL-3 containment level.
Knowledge of CDC and USDA import, export, transport, and permit requirements.
Experience with biological security, biosecurity, or biological risk management.
Experience with DOE directives, orders, laboratory operating contracts, or other federal research requirements.
Experience supporting the design, commissioning, or renovation of biological research facilities.
Experience developing data-driven program metrics and communicating program performance to senior leadership.
Experience supervising, mentoring, recruiting, or developing biosafety professionals.
Experience leading biosafety programs in a national laboratory or other highly regulated research environment.

Pay Range:
$240,960- $305,544 Annually

This is the lowest to highest salary range in good faith we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Additional Information

Position Information

This is a Career Indefinite position, open to Lab employees and external candidates.

Why Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory?

Included in 2026 Best Places to Work by Glassdoor!
Flexible Benefits Package
401(k)
Relocation Assistance
Education Reimbursement Program
Flexible schedules (*depending on project needs)
Our values - visit https://www.llnl.gov/inclusion/our-values

Security Clearance

This position requires a Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance. If you are selected, we will initiate a Federal background investigation to determine if you meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information or matter. Also, all L or Q cleared employees are subject to random drug testing. Q-level clearance requires U.S. citizenship.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

How To Identify Fake Job Advertisements

Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. LLNL never extends an offer without a personal interview and will never charge a fee for joining our company. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

To learn more about recruitment scams: https://www.llnl.gov/sites/www/files/2023-05/LLNL-Job-Fraud-Statement-Updated-4.26.23.pdf

Equal Employment Opportunity

We are an equal opportunity employer that is committed to providing all with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, protected veteran status, age, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Reasonable Accommodation

Our goal is to create an accessible and inclusive experience for all candidates applying and interviewing at the Laboratory. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please use our online form to submit a request.

California Privacy Notice

The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) grants privacy rights to all California residents. The law also entitles job applicants, employees, and non-employee workers to be notified of what personal information LLNL collects and for what purpose. The Employee Privacy Notice can be accessed here.

new_jobs.title: Fund Operations Analyst
new_jobs.description:
About Allocate

Allocate is building the operating system for private markets — wealth advisors and their clients use the platform to access, transact in, and manage private market investments. The platform supports 350+ advisory firms and 1,500+ GP relationships, with $5B+ in assets on the platform.

About The Role

As a Fund Operations Analyst, you will run the daily execution engine behind the 150+ funds on the Allocate platform. Capital call notices, wires and transfers, credit facility drawdowns, payment matching, expense reconciliation, and the records that everything else depends on.

As Allocate scales, the fund count on the platform is growing quickly, and we need to keep automating our processes to keep pace. You will learn the operational process, then work with the team and spearhead the efforts on how we can automate our workflows. This is a hands-on execution role with a build mandate attached, and you will be measured on two things. Did the work deliver a superb client experience, accurate and on time every time, and can the same team handle more funds this quarter than it could last quarter.

What You'll Own

You will work day to day alongside our Allocate Fund Finance team, splitting coverage across the fund portfolio, and report directly to the Head of Feeder Operations. You will also partner closely with our client service team, third-party fund administrators, audit and tax teams.

Fund Lifecycle Operations

Prepare capital call notices across the fund portfolio and route them for review and approval.
Set up wires and transfers across our banking platforms, including capital call fundings and distributions to limited and general partners.
Reconcile daily partner activity across bank accounts, flag anything that does not tie, and support quarterly cash queries from the fund administrator and auditors.
Own fund expense reconciliation. Code and allocate incoming invoices to the correct fund, series, and period, maintain and true up accruals, reconcile expenses against bank activity and the administrator’s books, and carry clean support into quarterly review and the annual audit.
Prepare credit facility drawdowns ahead of capital call deadlines, track repayments and outstanding balances, and pull together quarterly compliance reporting.
Own the core operational trackers covering investment activity, capital call payments, distributions, credit facilities, tax document status, and investor commitment records.
Review quarterly fund financials against source workpapers and tie the statements to the underlying schedules before anything goes out.
Assist in opening bank and brokerage accounts for new funds, including compiling the required entity documentation and maintaining account records.

Automation and Process

Document every workflow you touch and create new processes for those that don’t currently exist. If it is not written down, it cannot be audited, operationalized, improved, or automated.
Partner with Product and Engineering to push repeatable operational logic into the platform rather than keeping it in spreadsheets.
Build the automation. Templated notice generation, rules-based payment matching, invoice intake and expense allocation, self-updating accrual roll forwards, scheduled reconciliations, automatic file routing, and alerting on exceptions instead of manual daily checks.
Replace manual tracker updates with queries and dashboards pulled from the source systems.

What Success Looks Like

Capital calls, distributions, and wires go out accurately and on deadline, with no client-visible errors.
Expense reconciliation closes on schedule each period, with documented support that the administrator and auditors accept without a round of follow-up questions.
Manual hours come out of the core workflows every quarter, measured against the tasks you have automated or eliminated.
The fund count grows without a matching increase in operational headcount or cycle time.

Who You Are

1 to 3 years of experience in fund operations, fund administration, treasury, audit, or a related finance function, with a working understanding of private fund mechanics. Capital calls, distributions, fund expenses, capital accounts, and investor reporting.
Real reconciliation experience, and precision under deadline pressure. You have owned an expense or cash reconciliation before, you are comfortable explaining a variance to a reviewer, and you know that wire cutoffs and capital call dates do not move.
Process minded by instinct, and already using AI to take repetitive work off your plate. You write things down, you notice when the same problem shows up twice, and you fix the cause instead of the instance.
Strong communicator. You coordinate clearly with fund administrators, banks, auditors, and internal teams, and you keep people updated without being asked.
Growth-oriented and energized by a scaling environment. You want to grow with the firm and take on more ownership as the fund count and team expand.

Nice to Have

Experience working alongside a third-party fund administrator, reviewing and challenging their output rather than producing it yourself.
Treasury or payment operations background. Working in a bank portal with dual approval workflows, wire cutoffs, and payment controls.
Time in an early-stage or high-growth environment where the process did not exist yet and you had to build it.

Essential Values & Culture

Providing our clients with a world-class experience is our number one priority. We obsessively search for ways to improve the experience for our clients and partners. This requires extraordinary response times, proactivity, and ensuring that everything we do — from product strategy to offline communications — reflects a top-tier client experience.
Challenge convention: Instead of detailing all the reasons why an idea may not work, we constantly question things to determine how a viable idea may be put into motion.
Commitment to continuous improvement: We find ways to personally scale each day by pushing ourselves up the learning curve.
Meritocracy, not politics: We place the utmost value on results and rewards through merit, not reward actions driven by political agendas or behavior.
Civil Discourse is embraced: We believe open, intellectually curious conversations are required to consistently arrive at the best decisions. Respect is paramount in our dealings with one another, but our mission is always to get the right answer collectively, not to be right.
Embrace technological change: We adopt tools and techniques that make us faster, smarter, and better. We stay open to innovation, especially around AI and automation, and drop outdated methods without hesitation. This includes actively integrating AI-assisted tools into your daily workflow and staying current as the landscape evolves. Complacency kills progress — we value adaptability and curiosity.

Additional Details

Fully Hybrid Position
Travel may be required for company offsites
Broadband internet connection required
Location: All I-9 eligible candidates will be considered
Salary: $85,000 – $100,000 base, with bonus and equity eligibility
Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision; 401(k); and responsible vacation time (PTO)
Employment: Full-time

The base pay offered will be determined based on the candidate’s experience, location, skills, training, certifications, education, internal equity, and market data. Total compensation may also include a discretionary performance-based bonus. We do not anticipate that candidates hired will begin at the top of the range, though this may occur on a case-by-case basis.

new_jobs.title: Annotation Program Manager – AI/ML Data Operations
new_jobs.description:
About shift

shift pays everyday workers to record short videos of the tasks they already do (in kitchens,
workshops, job sites, bakeries, and warehouses) to help train the next generation of AI and
robotics. We’ve paid out over $15M to 25,000+ workers across 15+ countries.

About the role

We're looking for someone to own the quality bar for shift's egocentric training data - not to work to a
spec, but to write it. You'll own the golden sets, SOPs, and calibration system that every
annotator, reviewer, and auto-labeling model is measured against, and you'll work directly with
engineering to stand up new annotation workflows in hand tracking, object identification, and
action labelling. As we scale from thousands of contributors to millions, you're the reason the
99% accuracy bar holds. Your ground truth becomes the benchmark, and the model is
measured against it.

What you'll own

Own the quality bar end-to-end: golden/benchmark sets, acceptance criteria, frame-level tolerance thresholds, and the audit loops that hold them
Author, version, and continuously sharpen annotation SOPs, rubrics, and edge-case rules as the client spec evolves
Design and run inter-annotator agreement measurement (kappa/alpha, tolerance-based agreement on temporal boundaries) and publish regular quality reports
Analyse disagreement patterns to root cause - guideline ambiguity vs. annotator error - and fix the system, not just the file
Stand up the training and certification pipeline that brings new annotators and reviewers to the bar fast: onboarding, structured calibration sessions, targeted retraining
Design human-in-the-loop workflows where models pre-label and humans review, correct, and escalate - so output grows faster than headcount
Partner with engineering and product on new workflows: hand tracking (keypoints, left/right attribution, contact states), object identification (boxes/masks, ontology, naming consistency), action labelling (controlled vocabulary, segment boundaries)
Specify label schemas, annotation-tool requirements, and QC dashboards; validate pilot batches before production scaling
Run capacity planning across competing demands and allocate reviewer attention to the highest-impact work
Track acceptance/rejection, rework, and quality-adjusted productivity - and drive them week over week
Improve cost-per-accepted hour while protecting the bar; inform the in-house vs. vendor mix with quality data

What we're looking for

8+ years in AI/ML data annotation operations, including 4+ years managing annotation programs and teams (annotators, QA leads, managers)
5+ years of hands-on video annotation, including 1+ years with egocentric/first-person video for robotics or embodied AI - ideally at or for a leading robotics company or project
3+ years in a lead or QA capacity: calibrating annotators, adjudicating disagreements, and owning guidelines that others work on
Track record standing up 0→1 annotation programs and validating them through pilot to production
Deep command of quality methodology: IAA frameworks (kappa/alpha), gold-set creation, sampling strategies, tolerance thresholds - you can explain what a 99% (versus 95%) accuracy bar means in practice and design the system that holds it
Track record authoring (not just following) annotation SOPs and rubrics; able to translate ambiguous specs into precise, actionable guideline language
Hands-on with 2+ professional annotation tools - CVAT, Labelbox, Encord, V7, Label Studio, or equivalent - including configuring label schemas and QA workflows, not just annotating in them
Experience integrating model-based annotation into human workflows: auditing auto-generated labels and designing human-in-the-loop review that raises throughput without sacrificing quality
Outstanding written English - your rubrics train annotators and your labels are commands a model learns from
Strong analytical skills with Excel/Google Sheets for quality reporting
Data-driven, process-oriented mindset with strong ownership; startup-ready - comfortable with ambiguity, zero-to-one builds, and contributing when it matters most
Working understanding of ML and why annotation quality drives model performance
Bonus: Robotics, mechanical/mechatronics, or computer-vision engineering background; tier-1 institution or AI/robotics startup experience
Bonus:
Experience managing distributed/global annotator workforces or external vendors
Bonus:
Multi-modal annotation exposure: 3D/depth, joint pose, grasp outcome classification
Bonus:
Experience training or fine-tuning auto-labeling models, or partnering closely with the ML teams that do
Bonus:
Built annotation tooling or partnered tightly with a tooling team

About UGE

UGE is a full lifecycle renewable energy development company specializing in distributed generation and utility-scale solar PV and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). We develop, design, build, and operate clean energy assets across the United States from the first site assessment through to commercial operation. We're a mission-driven team that moves fast, solves hard problems, and is genuinely committed to accelerating the clean energy transition.

The Opportunity

The Senior Project Manager (SPM) is responsible for taking conceptual designs to operational reality. This role requires a deep understanding and experience in leading multiple complex projects simultaneously while supporting other Project Managers on their projects and shepherding their successes. This includes planning, scope delineation, design collaboration, procurement coordination, contracting, installation, and closeout/handoff to Portfolio Operations. The SPM creates and tracks project schedule progress against milestones, formulates and tracks full Development and EPC budget and payment forecasting needs, tracks and audits prevailing wage/certified payroll records for projects, and prepares identified reports to UGE Management.

The SPM must possess a comprehensive knowledge of C&I or community solar components, installation methods, quality control, best practices, AHJ/Utility process and communication requirements, regulatory standards, scheduling, budget tracking and forecasting, progress payment schedules, subcontracting, risk management, and closeout packages.

What You'll Do

Strategic Oversight And Leadership

Provides overarching leadership and strategic direction for multiple projects across any region(s).
Assumes responsibility (schedule and cost) for the successful completion of projects, from Notice to Proceed (NTP) to Commercial Operation Date (COD) and Portfolio Operations hand-off, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and objectives.

Advanced Contractual Management

Spearheads negotiations and final recommendations regarding contracts, playing a critical role in the recommendations and management of construction activities, consultants, and vendors.
Owns contractual oversight responsibilities on projects for major subcontractors, ensuring safety, compliance, quality, and efficiency.

Budget And Financial Management

Oversees the preservation and optimization of the IRR from the NTP budget approval stage through the handoff to Portfolio Operations.
Responsible for the overall EPC budget from NTP to Final Completion, making key decisions to preserve the as-modeled condition of the project.

Team Leadership And Development

Directly oversees internal resources for task management, providing leadership, mentorship, and support to other Project Managers.
Fosters professional development and growth within the team, offering guidance and coaching to lower levels of Project Managers and subordinate roles.
Acts as a role model, setting high standards and expectations for project execution and team performance.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Facilitates and enhances collaboration between Development, Engineering, Procurement, and Portfolio Operations teams, ensuring cohesiveness and alignment in project execution.
Leads critical meetings and discussions, representing the project team in high-level strategic meetings and decision-making processes.

Quality And Compliance Assurance

Ensures that all projects adhere to industry standards, legal regulations, and company policies.
Implements and oversees quality control measures, consistently monitoring project progress and performance.
Ensures Certified payroll for contractors is collected and properly certified for regulations.

Risk Management And Mitigation

Identifies potential risks and challenges at the regional level, developing and implementing effective mitigation strategies.
Holds ultimate accountability for resolving high-level issues and challenges that arise during project execution.

Stakeholder Engagement And Communication

Maintains strong relationships with key stakeholders, including clients, vendors, partners, Utilities, Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs), and other regulatory bodies.
Ensures effective and transparent communication across all levels of the project team and external entities.

Travel : 15-25% Travel to Project Sites

Who You'll Work With

Reports to Managing Director, Project Execution
Manages multiple external parties as needed to complete projects successfully.

Work Location & Schedule

This is an onsite hybrid position. Candidates are expected to work from our New York City office four days per week, with one work-from-home day each week. Candidates who are not currently located within commuting distance of either office must be willing to relocate. Relocation assistance is not provided.

What We're Looking For

Bachelor’s degree in engineering or other quantitative educational background, or equivalent experience.
A minimum of 6 years of relevant solar or energy storage project management experience (Solar PV, Energy Storage, or Electrical sectors)
Superior oral and written communication skills, tailored for higher-level stakeholder engagement.
Advanced ability to drive project teams and entities to success, ensuring deadlines and goals are met.
Leadership in fostering a collaborative environment and proactive approach to seeking information and research.
Expert in complex problem-solving abilities, including navigating challenging project scenarios and leading innovative solutions.
Detail oriented while capable of seeing and understanding the full picture.
Collaborate as part of a broader project management team to include, mentor, and develop others.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us

Competitive and thoughtfully structured compensation package, including a strong base salary that reflects your experience and the impact you bring to the role.
Fully paid Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage, your health and peace of mind come first.
401(k) with employer match, helping you grow your financial future.
Generous PTO time so you can unplug, recharge, and take care of what matters most.
Join a smart, collaborative, mission‑driven team that’s actively accelerating the transition to a clean‑energy future and making a real impact on the health of our planet.

Our Commitment to Inclusion

Compensation will be based on experience, education, and other relevant factors. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. UGE is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Themed Experiences
new_jobs.description:
Teamwork makes the stream work.  
Roku is changing how the world watches TV
Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.
From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.

What does the team work on? Roku’s Viewer Product team owns the ever-evolving end-to-end experience for the 100+ million households that use Roku every day. We design, build, and optimize everything they see—from the Roku Home Screen, Live TV Guide, and Sports Zone to the Roku Channel app on and off-platform—and power it all with our Consumer-AI personalization engine, which is also used for these experiences, as well as the billions of searches performed. Our global, cross-functional squad of product managers, designers, data scientists, and engineers spans San Jose, New York, Santa Monica, Austin, Boston, the UK, Mexico, and India. Our mission is to connect 400 million viewers worldwide to their favorite entertainment through something that is simple and delightful.

What is the role? Roku is seeking a Senior Program Manager, Themed Experiences to join the Viewer Product team and help bring to life a new, high-visibility surface on the Roku Home Screen. This is a highly visible, leadership-level program.
This role will drive the program toward launch, coordinating across engineering, product management, advertising, personalization, and creative teams to deliver a differentiated Roku experience.
The Senior Program Manager will build and maintain program structure, manage cross-functional dependencies spanning multiple time zones, and ensure the team hits critical milestones on an ambitious timeline. This person will also partner with stakeholders to develop tooling and scheduling workflows for content creators, enabling a sustainable and scalable production process. The ideal candidate is a seasoned program leader who thrives in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, earns trust through decisive action, and brings recommendations on AI-driven automations and methodologies to optimize program execution.
For California, New York, and Massachusetts - The estimated annual base salary for this position is between $280,000 - $310,000 annually. Compensation packages are based on factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, certifications, and specific geographical location. This role is eligible for health insurance, equity awards, life insurance, disability benefits, parental leave, wellness benefits, and paid time off.

How will I use AI at Roku? At Roku, we don't just use AI; we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability.
We value curious, adaptable builders who can show how they've used AI, agents, or automation to move faster, improve quality, and scale their impact. Strong candidates know how to frame problems, guide AI-assisted work, check the output, and learn quickly. Above all, they bring curiosity, adaptability, and sound judgment.

What are the responsibilities of the role? Drive end-to-end program management for a new home screen experience from development through launch and ongoing operations
Coordinate cross-functional workstreams across product, engineering, design, advertising, personalization, and creative teams
Build and maintain detailed program plans, timelines, and dependency maps across globally distributed teams spanning multiple time zones
Establish and run program governance including status reporting, risk identification, escalation paths, and decision-making frameworks
Partner with product management to translate vision into actionable milestones and deliverables
Develop tooling requirements and scheduling workflows for content creators to enable scalable production
Drive alignment across senior stakeholders, ensuring clarity of roles, responsibilities, and priorities
Identify and implement process improvements, including AI-powered automations and methodologies, to accelerate program delivery
Manage competing priorities and make timely trade-off decisions to keep the program on track
Leverage project management tools such as Jira, Jira Product Discovery, and Asana to maintain program visibility and accountability

What experience would help someone be successful in this role at Roku? 10+ years of program management experience in technology, media, entertainment, or consumer products
Demonstrated success managing
Experience driving programs from concept through launch in fast-paced, ambiguous environments
Strong ability to earn trust and influence without direct authority across engineering, product, design, and creative teams
Proficiency with project management and product discovery tools such as Jira, Asana, and similar platforms
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to synthesize information for diverse audiences
Experience working with globally distributed teams across multiple time zones
Familiarity with consumer-facing product development, home screen or platform experiences, or content-driven product surfaces
Track record of identifying and implementing process efficiencies, including the use of AI tools and automation
Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities

What's Roku's approach to hybrid working?
Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.

What are some of the benefits?
Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits include global access to mental health and financial wellness support and resources. Local benefits include statutory and voluntary benefits which may include healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), life, accident, disability, commuter, and retirement options (401(k)/pension). Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. It's important to note that not every benefit is available in all locations or for every role. For details specific to your location, please consult with your recruiter.

Accommodations
Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries to EmployeeRelations@Roku.com.

What should I know about Roku's culture?
Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV. 
We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. We come up with the solution, but the solution isn't real until it is built and delivered to the customer. That penchant for action gives us a pragmatic approach to innovation, one that has served us well since 2002. 
To learn more about Roku, our global footprint, and how we've grown, visit https://www.weareroku.com/factsheet.
By providing your information, you acknowledge that you want Roku to contact you about job roles, that you have read Roku's Applicant Privacy Notice, and understand that Roku will use your information as described in that notice. If you do not wish to receive any communications from Roku regarding this role or similar roles in the future, you may unsubscribe at any time by emailing WorkforcePrivacy@Roku.com.

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, B2G Operations
new_jobs.description:
Parallel Defense
is an executive strategic advisory, go-to-market, and business-development firm that helps high-growth commercial and dual-use technology companies enter and scale within the U.S. Government, defense, aerospace, and national-security markets.
We work as an extension of our clients’ commercial organizations. Our team develops government-market strategy, identifies and qualifies opportunities, builds relationships with government stakeholders and industry partners, supports capture and partnership development, and helps clients establish a practical, repeatable B2G growth capability.
Our work is founder-led, high-trust, fast-moving, and highly collaborative. We value judgment, discretion, clear writing, professional follow-through, and a strong bias toward real commercial outcomes.

Role Description:

Parallel Defense is seeking a highly organized and disciplined Program Manager, B2G Operations
to run the day-to-day operational engine behind our work. This is a founder-side role: you will work directly with the Founder & CEO on active client engagements - ensuring every meeting, deliverable, deadline, and workflow is tracked, prepared, and communicated with precision.
The Program Manager coordinates complex, cross-functional work across internal and external stakeholders. You will manage client engagement timelines and workflows, keep up-to-date records and statuses for deliverables, milestones, materials, and requirements, and accompany the CEO to client and stakeholder meetings. You will facilitate opportunity tracking and follow-ups, conduct high-level market research, provide progress reporting, and keep us on course. You will maintain awareness of teammates’ projects/deliverables, champion organization through Asana and Google Workspace, and handle additional operational needs.
Public sector experience is a plus but not required. You must be sharp, reliable, punctual, detail-oriented, adaptable, and efficient - able to move between project management, client service, research support, and operational execution without dropping details.
This role is ideal for someone who is comfortable in fast-paced startup environments and wants to gain experience in the defense industry and learn government contracting operations.

Core Responsibilities:

1) Client Delivery & Account Support

Serve as the day-to-day execution partner to the Founder & CEO on assigned client engagements.
Own the tracking and management of client engagement timelines, milestones, and deliverables.
Build and maintain integrated timelines, workflows, and project trackers in Asana and Google Workspace: initiatives, milestones, deliverables, owners, dependencies, deadlines, and approval points.
Coordinate and prepare for weekly client working sessions: pre-reads, materials, action items, and follow-up communications.
Facilitate client onboarding, including collection of materials, contact organization, and government administrative set up.
Assist with federal compliance parameters and requirements, tracking progress, identifying blockers, and flagging executive review when necessary.
Coordinate inputs from clients’ internal teams - including stakeholders across commercial sales, marketing, product, technical teams, legal, contracts, security, compliance, finance, procurement, operations, and executive leadership.
Ensure client deliverables are polished, accurate, organized, on time, and ready for senior review.
Maintain structured document storage, version control, templates, and repeatable delivery workflows.
Prepare monthly client status reports, progress summaries, and executive-review materials.
Track receivables and deliverables status with client internal teams; flag payment milestones, invoice triggers, and scope risks early and elevate them to the Founder & CEO.

2) Government BD & Capture Operations

Assist the CEO and Government Business Development team’s capture operations by organizing and maintaining the opportunity pipeline, CRM and contact data, account status, onboarding data collection and management.
Prepare presentation materials and meeting briefs for government, prime-contractor, integrator, and executive conversations.
Facilitate follow-ups after external meetings.
Track next steps and deliverables and maintain updated records in Asana and Google Workspace with clear accountability for each task.
Track opportunity-specific readiness items involving product, technical, security, legal, contracts, procurement, finance, and operations teams.
Support the CEO and Government Business Development team with timely coordination, preparation, and follow-through on BD and capture activities.

3) Client Capture Support

Support incoming client capture efforts with research, materials, meetings, and pipeline management.
Prepare presentation materials and meeting briefs for client discovery meetings and executive conversations.
Draft and coordinate approved outreach, follow-up notes, and internal relationship updates.
Track conversations, commitments, open questions, and next actions across incoming client opportunities.
Help ensure that engagement activity remains tied to defined client strategy, target accounts, and realistic commercial outcomes.

4) Parallel Org Management & Executive Operations

Track team workflows, priorities, and deliverables across Parallel’s internal projects and initiatives.
Support research and planning for conferences and events; coordinate logistics, travel arrangements, and internal prep.
Maintain internal operating rhythms: team stand-ups, leadership check-ins, and all-hands prep.
Own Asana & Google Workspace hygiene for internal projects: tasks, dependencies, custom fields, dashboards, and weekly status views.
Produce weekly internal reports: milestone completion, risks/blockers, upcoming deadlines, and capacity load across teammates’ projects.
Standardize operating rhythms (checklists, templates, SOPs) to scale delivery quality.

Qualifications

5-8 years of experience in operations, program management, client delivery, professional services, or related roles (startup or high-growth B2B environment preferred).
Exceptional organization and follow-through across multiple workstreams, stakeholders, deadlines, and documents.
Strong written communication skills; able to produce polished executive-facing briefs, presentations, emails, meeting notes, and research summaries.
Strong research and analytical skills; able to turn imperfect information into clear, decision-useful documents.
Professional judgment, discretion, and comfort handling confidential client information.
Strong client-service mindset and ability to communicate clearly with senior executives and technical subject-matter experts.
Comfort working in a small, fast-moving, founder-led environment where responsibilities evolve quickly.
Extreme comfort and proficiency with AI tools (e.g., Perplexity, Claude, ChatGPT)—used efficiently and with discretion.
Proficiency with Google Workspace, Asana, presentation tools, spreadsheets, project-management tools, and research workflows.

Preferred:
Exposure to federal/defense/aerospace/public-sector, dual-use technology, or government operations; experience supporting BD, account planning, sales operations, or professional-services delivery; ability to travel periodically.

The Project Manager, Technology Delivery leads the planning and delivery of cross-functional technology and business initiatives for the Specialty Food Association (SFA).
